In support of this thesis, the Committee cites the data derived from its study of 18 model cities (see Table 1, supra). These data were compiled from questionnaires sent to unidentified members of the academic community and purport to show the low level of economic interaction between base municipalities and their surrounding suburbs. We have serious questions concerning the methodology employed in this study, however, and, in any event, we are not persuaded that it undermines the general conclusions reached in the Interim Report. First of all, it appears that the scope of information garnered about each model city was rather limited in that only a single questionnaire was completed with respect to each city studied. Furthermore, there is no indication of the sources of information used by those completing the questionnaire. We are left with several fundamental questions: Was this information gleaned from governmental or local interest sources (e.g., United States Bureau of Census, chambers of commerce)? Were transportation users (shippers) consulted? Are the quoted statistics the result of estimates made by those solicited? Some doubts are raised by the characterizations given some of the responses. In particular, the Committee states that the study indicates no measurable or significant business relocation from Richmond to its proposed commercial zone area over the past 10 years. 28
28 
For the 18 studied cities there was negligible business relocation reported except with respect to Des Moines, Iowa, where an estimated 10 percent of the municipally based business firms relocated to the surrounding area. The scope and meaning of the term "business" is not defined by the Committee.
